rationale: Genuine no-spec round (no story/spec artifact, acceptance not dispatched) caps confidence at low. 3 blocking findings survived triage: a stale AnalyticsGuard docstring misstating the access boundary (standards-flagged, CR-001); custom-dashboard management now reachable by any authenticated user once the outer Enterprise/admin gate was removed, with no remaining role check (security, ambiguous under no-spec so kept as patch, CR-002); and a redirect effect that no longer waits for feature-flag config to load before evicting deep-linked tabs (CR-003). 5 findings dismissed as noise (the auth-only page widening and unconditional Insights/CLI-Insights tabs match the task's own stated scope, the deleted METRICS_ANALYTICS constant has zero remaining references, one branch is now dead code, one race is pre-existing and unaffected by this diff). 0 deferred.

standards_review.notes: No code-quality.md standards guide in this repo and no code-quality ArtifactRef was passed
AnalyticsGuard.tsx:24-27 docstring still claims a role check gates the guard; isAnalyticsAccessible is now auth-only. See CR-001.

findings.title: Stale docstring misrepresents access boundary
findings.problem: AnalyticsGuard's JSDoc (lines 24-27) still says the guard 'combines Enterprise Edition with the standalone CLI Analytics feature flag plus a global/project-admin role check (see isAnalyticsAccessible)', but isAnalyticsAccessible (src/utils/analyticsAccess.ts:22) was changed in this same diff to `user !== null` — no flag or role check remains.
findings.impact: A future contributor trusts the stale comment and assumes a role/flag check already gates this route, risking an access-control regression built on a false assumption about the real security boundary.
findings.recommendation: Update the AnalyticsGuard docstring to state the guard is now auth-only, matching isAnalyticsAccessible's actual behavior.

findings.title: Custom dashboard management now reachable by any user
findings.problem: isCustomizationEnabled (line 50) is only `useFeatureFlag('feature:dashboardCustomization')` — it never carried an admin/project-admin role check. It was previously gated by an isMetricsAnalyticsEnabled conjunct (removed at AnalyticsPage.tsx:102,118 and AnalyticsDashboard.tsx:149) and by the page-level isAnalyticsAccessible check, which required Enterprise Edition or an admin/project-admin role with CLI Analytics enabled. Both outer gates are now gone: isAnalyticsAccessible collapsed to `user !== null`, and the metricsAnalytics conjunct was dropped from the customization gate.
findings.impact: Any authenticated, non-admin user can now view, edit, and manage shared custom dashboards wherever the dashboardCustomization flag is on for a tenant — a real authorization widening with no role check anywhere in the remaining chain.
findings.recommendation: Confirm this is intended; if not, add an explicit role check (isAdmin || isProjectAdmin) to isCustomizationEnabled or to the dashboard-management actions themselves. No spec exists to resolve the ambiguity, so this is flagged for explicit confirmation rather than assumed safe.

findings.title: Redirect effect no longer waits for flag config to load
findings.problem: The stale-tab redirect effect previously returned early via `if (!isMetricsAnalyticsLoaded) return`. Because isConfigFetched is a single global flag shared by every useFeatureFlag call, that guard effectively gated the whole effect on the shared feature-flag config having loaded. It is deleted outright with no replacement, so the effect now runs immediately on mount, before isCliAnalyticsEnabled/isLeaderboardEnabled/isCustomizationEnabled resolve from their false defaults.
findings.impact: A user who deep-links to a tab gated by a still-loading flag (CLI Analytics, Leaderboard, or a custom dashboard) is redirected via `replace: true` to Insights before the flag resolves true, silently losing the deep link even after the flag finishes loading.
findings.recommendation: Gate the redirect effect on the shared config-loaded state (e.g. destructure isLoaded from one of the useFeatureFlag calls) before evaluating whether the active tab is missing from the list.
